headline: Standardized cross-dataset benchmarks are reshaping how biomedical ML methods are validated
label: Validation Design In Biomedical Prediction
summary: Biomedical ML claims increasingly rest on cross-dataset and cross-platform benchmarks rather than single-cohort validation.
synthesis: The common thread is evaluation design as a determinant of claimed performance in biomedical machine learning. PRTS assesses in-context prediction of clinical endpoints from bulk transcriptomes across diseases and platforms, without per-cohort training. TabBioMed standardizes comparison across 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets with standardized preprocessing, evaluating 23 models, where foundation models lead. Elflow pairs automated quality control with VICReg-based self-supervised representation learning and is benchmarked on public flow and CyTOF datasets. What is new is the pairing of method claims with standardized benchmarking across datasets or platforms, rather than validation confined to a single cohort. Whether these benchmarks generalize beyond their curated sources is not established by the items.
